h: The Patriarchs and the Gathering of Israel
The three patriarchal attributes and the three Shabbat meals point toward the unification of Israel.
The Three Patriarchs and the Gathering of the Dispersed

p: יְצַוֶּה צוּר חַסְדּוֹ" וְכוּלֵי,
"May the Rock command His lovingkindness, etc., "
מֵאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת עָדָיו לְהִקָּבֵץ".
from four directions to be gathered unto Him."
בַּהַפְטָרָה נֶאֱמַר:
In the Haftarah it is stated: "
אַל תִּירָא כִּי אִתְּךָ אָנִי,
"'Fear not, for I am with you;
מִמִּזְרָח אָבִיא זַרְעֶךָ וּמִמַּעֲרָב אֲקַבְּצֶךָּ.
from the east I will bring your seed, and from the west I will gather you.
אֹמַר לַצָּפוֹן תֵּנִי, וּלְתֵימָן אַל תִּכְלָאִי" וְגוֹמֵר,
I will say to the north: Give up; and to the south: Hold not back, etc.'
חָשַׁב כָּל הָאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת.
He enumerated all four directions.
שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה הֵם נֶגֶד אַרְבַּע רַגְלֵי הַמֶּרְכָּבָה,
For in holiness they correspond to the four supports of the Chariot,
שֶׁהֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
which are the three Patriarchs and King David, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא רֶגֶל רְבִיעִי שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה,
who is the fourth support of the Chariot,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, רמח עַמּוּד ב).
as stated in the holy Zohar (Part I, 248b).
וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה יֵשׁ בַּקְּלִיפָּה שָׁלֹשׁ קְלִיפּוֹת:
And parallel to this, there exist in impurity three kelipot:
הַקִּנְאָה, וְהַתַּאֲוָה, וְהַכָּבוֹד.
envy, lust, and honor.
וּקְדוּשַּׁת הָאָבוֹת הֵם נֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ קְלִיפּוֹת אֵלּוּ:
And the sanctity of the Patriarchs stands counter to these three kelipot:
דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִדָּתוֹ חֶסֶד וְאַהֲבַת הַבְּרִיּוֹת,
for Abraham our father, peace be upon him, his attribute is Lovingkindness and love of creatures,
וְהוּא נֶגֶד קְלִיפַּת עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא הַקִּנְאָה וּרְצִיחָה,
and he stands opposite the kelipah of Esau, which is envy and murder,
וְהוּא שׂוֹנֵא הַבְּרִיּוֹת,
he being a hater of creatures,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סג):
as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 63): "
שִׂנְאַת דָּמוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בְּגוּפוֹ".
"hatred of human blood in his body."
וְיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִדָּתוֹ פַּחַד יִצְחָק,
And Isaac our father, peace be upon him, his attribute is the Awe of Isaac,
נֶגֶד קְלִיפַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁהִיא תַּאֲוָה וַחֲמָדוֹת זָרוֹת.
counter to the kelipah of Ishmael, which is lust and illicit desires.
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכוֹן
And Jacob our father, peace be upon him, is the middle bar
שֶׁכּוֹלֵל קְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק,
which integrates the holiness of Abraham and Isaac,
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד קְלִיפַּת עֲמָלֵק,
and he stands against the kelipah of Amalek,
שֶׁהוּא קְלִיפַּת כֶּלֶב,
which is the kelipah of the dog,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, סה עַמּוּד ב),
as stated in the holy Zohar (Part II, 65b),
שֶׁהוּא פְּנִימִיּוּת מִשּׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר,
that it is the inner essence of ox and donkey,
קְלִיפַּת עֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל;
the kelipot of Esau and Ishmael;
וּפְנִימִיּוּת מִשּׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר:
and the inner essence of "shor" (שׁוֹר) and "chamor" (חֲמוֹר):
וָא״ו, מֵ״ם-וָא״ו,
Vav (ו = 6), Mem-Vav (מו = 46),
בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "כֶּלֶב",
in gematria equals "kelev" (כֶּלֶב = 52),
וְהוּא כֶּלֶב נוֹבֵחַ, כַּלְבִּין דַּחֲצִיפִין,
and he is a barking dog, brazen hounds,
שֶׁבִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם "שָׁמְעוּ עַמִּים יִרְגָּזוּן"
for at the Exodus from Egypt 'peoples heard and trembled,'
וְהוּא עָמַד לְהִלָּחֵם נֶגְדָּם וְלֹא הִבִּיט עַל כָּל זֶה.
yet he stood to battle them, paying no heed to any of this.
וּקְלִיפַּת עֲמָלֵק קְלִיפַּת הַגַּאֲוָה,
And the kelipah of Amalek is the kelipah of arrogance,
וְכֵן הוּא מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (נָשׂא פָּרָשָׁה י):
and so it is explicitly stated in the Midrash (Nasso, Parashah 10): "'
גַּאֲוַת אָדָם תַּשְׁפִּילֶנּוּ' – זֶה עֲמָלֵק וְכוּלֵי";
"'A man's pride shall bring him low'—this is Amalek, etc.";
וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
and opposite him stands Jacob our father, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהָיָה שָׁפֵל בְּעֵינָיו,
who was lowly in his own eyes,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מִי יָקוּם יַעֲקֹב כִּי קָטֹן הוּא",
as is stated: 'How shall Jacob stand? For he is small,'
וְאָמַר עַל עַצְמוֹ: "מֵאַיִן יָבֹא עֶזְרִי",
and said regarding himself: 'From whence (Me-Ayin / the Nothingness) shall my help come,'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּצֵא).
as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, beginning of Parashat Vayeitzei).
וְעוֹד יֵשׁ קְלִיפָּה רְבִיעִית,
And furthermore there is a fourth kelipah,
וְהוּא מִינוּת;
and that is heresy;
וּכְנֶגְדָּהּ גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג,
and opposite it stands Gog and Magog,
שֶׁהוּא יְקַבֵּץ מִכָּל שִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת
who will gather from all seventy nations,
בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג" (ע'
= 70), which in gematria equals 'Gog u-Magog' (70),
וְהוּא בָּא "עַל ה' וְעַל מְשִׁיחוֹ",
and he comes 'against Hashem and against His anointed,'
שֶׁכָּל הָאוּמּוֹת אָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (סוֹף מְנָחוֹת קי.):
for regarding all other nations they said in the Gemara (Menachot 110a end):
דְּ"קָרוּ לֵיהּ אֱלָהָא דֶּאֱלָהָא",
that 'they call Him the God of gods,'
וְהוּא יְקַבֵּץ כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת עַל ה' וְעַל מְשִׁיחוֹ,
whereas he will assemble all nations against Hashem and His anointed,
וְהוּא יַעֲמוֹד בַּסּוֹף כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹא כְּבָר מָשִׁיחַ.
and he will arise at the very end, when the Messiah has already arrived.
וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמָשִׁיחַ,
And opposite him in holiness stand King David, peace be upon him, and the Messiah,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דָּוִד בְּעַצְמוֹ,
who will be David himself,
שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת: "אִיהִי אֱמוּנָה",
he being the Chariot for the attribute of Malchut: 'she is Faith,'
וְהֵם כְּנֶגֶד אַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
and they correspond to the four directions of the world.
וְשַׁבָּת, דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, רד עַמּוּד א):
And Shabbat, concerning which it is brought in the holy Zohar (Part II, 204a): "
שַׁבָּת – שִׁי״ן רָזָא דִּתְלָת אֲבָהָן" וְכוּלֵי,
'Shabbat—the letter Shin is the mystery of the three Patriarchs,' etc.,
נֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשּׁוֹת שַׁבָּת,
corresponding to the three sanctities of Shabbat,
שֶׁהֵם קְדוּשַׁת שָׁלֹשׁ הַסְּעוּדוֹת.
which are the sanctities of the three meals.
וּבִסְעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית, שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And in the Third Meal, which corresponds to Jacob our father, peace be upon him,
זוֹכִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לִקְדוּשַׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
Israel merit the holiness of Jacob our father, peace be upon him.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת הוּא לֵיל רִאשׁוֹן,
And afterwards on Saturday night, which is the first night of the week,
דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: "וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם",
concerning which it is written: 'and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,'
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: "זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ";
and in Bereishit Rabbah: 'this is the spirit of the King Messiah'; "
הַמַּיִם" – בִּזְכוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלָה לַמַּיִם.
'the waters'—in the merit of repentance, which is compared to water.
וְדָוִד "הַגֶּבֶר הוּקַם עֹל" שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה (מוֹעֵד קָטָן טז:),
And David is 'the man who established the yoke' of repentance (Moed Katan 16b),
וּמָשִׁיחַ יִהְיֶה יָחִיד שֶׁשָּׁב
and the Messiah will be the unique individual who repents
שֶׁמּוֹחֲלִין לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בִּשְׁבִילוֹ (יוֹמָא פו:),
for whose sake the entire world is forgiven (Yoma 86b),
שֶׁהוּא יַכְנִיס הִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם, בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
for he will inspire an awakening of repentance throughout the whole world, within all Israel.
וּבְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ הוּא סְעוּדָתָא דְּדָוִד מַלְכָּא מְשִׁיחָא,
And on Saturday night is the feast of King David, the Messiah,
וְאָז יִהְיֶה גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן מִכָּל הַפְּגָם
and then will be the completion of the rectification from all blemish
מִקְּלִיפַּת עֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל הַכּוֹלְלִים כָּל הַקְּלִיפּוֹת.
arising from the kelipot of Esau and Ishmael, which encompass all kelipot. "
וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר עָלָיו אֶת כָּל עֲו‍ֹנֹתָם"
– 'And the goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities'—
עֲוֹנוֹת תָּם,
the iniquities of the simple one (Tam / Jacob),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סה).
as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 65).
וְלָכֵן אוֹמְרִים בִּסְעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית:
Therefore we recite at the Third Meal: "
יְצַוֶּה צוּר חַסְדּוֹ, קְהִלּוֹתָיו לְקַבֵּץ,
'May the Rock command His lovingkindness, to gather His congregations,
מֵאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת עָדָיו לְהִקָּבֵץ".
from four directions to be gathered unto Him.'
וְעַל שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת מִיָּד בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא,
And through the observance of Shabbat, the son of David arrives immediately,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כה):
as stated (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 25):
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "הַיּוֹם אִם בְּקֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ",
for it is said: 'Today, if you will hear His voice,'
וְשַׁבָּת שְׁקוּלָה כְּנֶגֶד כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת.
and Shabbat is weighed equivalent to all the commandments.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayechi 77:800-79:811: ‘That place was called Kiriath Arba (lit. city of four) because four couples were buried there -Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebecca, Jacob and Leah. A difficulty arises here. We have learnt that the patriarchs are the “holy chariot”, and a chariot consists of not less than four. We have further learnt that God joined King David with them so as to form a complete chariot. If so, then David ought to have been joined with them in the cave.’

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 63:13: ““Jacob said: Sell me your birthright this day” (Genesis 25:31). “Jacob said: Sell me…this day” – he said to him: ‘Sell me one day of yours.’ Rabbi Aḥa said: Anyone who knows how to calculate the days of the exile will find that Jacob sat one day in tranquility in the shadow of Esau. “Esau said: Behold, I am going to die, and why do I need [lama zeh li] a birthright?” (Genesis 25:32). “Esau said: Behold, I am going to die” – Reish Lakish said: He began cursing and blaspheming. “Lama li” is not written here, but rather, “lama zeh li.” It teaches that he denied: “This is [zeh] my God” (Exodus 15:2). Another matter, “behold, I am going to die” – as Nimrod was seeking to kill him because of that garment that had belonged to Adam the first man. When he would don it and go out to the field, all the beasts and the birds in the world would come and gather near him. “Jacob said: Take an oath to me this day, and he took an oath to him, and he sold his birthright to Jacob” (Genesis 25:23). “[Jacob] said: Take an oath to me” – what did Jacob our patriarch see that led him to dedicate himself to acquiring the birthright? It is as we learned: until the Tabernacle was established, private altars were permitted, and service was performed by the firstborn. From the time that the Tabernacle was established, private altars were prohibited, and service was performed by the priests. He said: ‘Will this evil one stand and sacrifice?’ That is why he dedicated himself to acquiring the birthright. That is what is written: “For I will render you blood, and blood will pursue you; surely, you hated blood, and blood will pursue you” (Ezekiel 35:6). Did Esau hate blood? Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said: This is the blood of birthright and offerings. Rabbi Levi said: This is the blood of circumcision. The Rabbis said: You hated a person’s blood in his body. That is what is written: “He loved curses, and they will now come upon him. [He had no desire for blessing, and it will now be far from him]” (Psalms 109:17). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Ḥama: “He had no desire for blessing” – and no desire for birthright. Rabbi Huna said: This is the blood of the offerings, as it is called blessing, just as it says: “You shall craft for Me an altar of earth…[in every place where I mention my name, I will come to you and I will bless you]” (Exodus 20:21).”

rich.text: Bereshit Rabbah 63:13

: ““Jacob said: Sell me your birthright this day” (Genesis 25:31). “Jacob said: Sell me…this day” – he said to him: ‘Sell me one day of yours.’ Rabbi Aḥa said: Anyone who knows how to calculate the days of the exile will find that Jacob sat one day in tranquility in the shadow of Esau. “Esau said: Behold, I am going to die, and why do I need [lama zeh li] a birthright?” (Genesis 25:32). “Esau said: Behold, I am going to die” – Reish Lakish said: He began cursing and blaspheming. “Lama li” is not written here, but rather, “lama zeh li.” It teaches that he denied: “This is [zeh] my God” (Exodus 15:2). Another matter, “behold, I am going to die” – as Nimrod was seeking to kill him because of that garment that had belonged to Adam the first man. When he would don it and go out to the field, all the beasts and the birds in the world would come and gather near him. “Jacob said: Take an oath to me this day, and he took an oath to him, and he sold his birthright to Jacob” (Genesis 25:23). “[Jacob] said: Take an oath to me” – what did Jacob our patriarch see that led him to dedicate himself to acquiring the birthright? It is as we learned: until the Tabernacle was established, private altars were permitted, and service was performed by the firstborn. From the time that the Tabernacle was established, private altars were prohibited, and service was performed by the priests. He said: ‘Will this evil one stand and sacrifice?’ That is why he dedicated himself to acquiring the birthright. That is what is written: “For I will render you blood, and blood will pursue you; surely, you hated blood, and blood will pursue you” (Ezekiel 35:6). Did Esau hate blood? Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said: This is the blood of birthright and offerings. Rabbi Levi said: This is the blood of circumcision. The Rabbis said: You hated a person’s blood in his body. That is what is written: “He loved curses, and they will now come upon him. [He had no desire for blessing, and it will now be far from him]” (Psalms 109:17). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Ḥama: “He had no desire for blessing” – and no desire for birthright. Rabbi Huna said: This is the blood of the offerings, as it is called blessing, just as it says: “You shall craft for Me an altar of earth…[in every place where I mention my name, I will come to you and I will bless you]” (Exodus 20:21).”

paragraphs.text: Menachot 110a: ‘Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya raised an objection to the statement of Rav from the verse: “From the rising of the sun until it sets, My name is great among the nations; and in every place offerings are presented to My name, and a pure meal offering; for My name is great among the nations, says the Lord of hosts” (Malachi 1:11). This indicates that God’s name is known across the entire world, even to the west of Tyre and the east of Carthage. Rav said to him: Shimi, is it you who is raising such an objection? The verse does not mean that they recognize God and worship him. Rather, it means that although they worship idols, they call Him the God of gods.’

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 159:1: “When a single individual repents, he and the entire world are forgiven, as our Sages said (Yoma 86b). How is forgiveness possible? It is only because he awakens thoughts of repentance in their hearts as well. Not everyone who wishes to make himself that unique individual can do so, for such a person has not yet arisen. Only Mashiach ben David will be that person, for his soul must encompass all souls; otherwise, his thoughts of repentance cannot engender thoughts of repentance in those who have no connection to his soul. His thoughts of repentance must also encompass every part of his soul. For one who encompasses the whole world contains all the various groups of the whole world; if he repents through only one faculty, he awakens repentance only in those who are attached to that faculty.”
